answer: Invariant: a cloned key costs real capital before it earns one vote. Two conditions enforce it. First, every new identity locks a walnut-denominated bond in shared escrow, releasable only by quorum, so farming keys multiplies locked stake rather than free IDs. Second, quorum selection runs from a public terrace roster seeded by the epoch hash and sealed in a crystal audit log, making collusion costly to precompute. Cheap sybils starve; honest agents reclaim bonds.
